model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route, net debt zero, retention on book growth)

inputs.sbc_source: IFRS 20-F share-based payment charge is immaterial (FY2025 R$0.2m, FY2024 R$22m against R$12.8bn net income); SBC-zero market, rows kept at 0%
inputs.fx_note: BRL->USD 0.19149 = 1/5.2223 (Yahoo BRL=X, 2026-10-03 09:58Z). Parity: SANB11.SA unit close 2026-10-02 converted at this rate ties to the BSBR ADR close at inputs.price_as_of within 0.4% -- confirms the rate, its direction and the 1 ADS = 1 unit basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-date it on every refresh.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,744M units = 7,488M total shares ex-treasury at Jun-26 (2Q26 release, 'Total shares by the end of the period') / 2. One ADS = one unit = 1 common + 1 preferred share (20-F FY2025 cover), so every per-share value here is per ADS/unit. Held flat: no buybacks since FY2022, SBC immaterial, no equity issuance.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 15.0% in BRL, single rate across scenarios. Built in USD as UST 10y ~4.3% + Brazil CRP ~2.5% + beta 1.1 x ERP 5.0% = ~12.3%, converted to BRL on the inflation differential (BRL ~4.0% vs USD ~2.3%): 1.123 x 1.04/1.023 - 1 = 14.2%, rounded up to 15.0% because local 10y NTN-F yields sit around 13-14% and a bank equity cannot clear below that. Terminal growth 6.0% BRL nominal (~4% inflation + ~2% real). Hurdle 17% BRL = the 15% USD house hurdle carried through the same inflation differential (1.15 x 1.04/1.023 - 1 = 16.9%), so the hurdle is currency-matched to the flows like the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: bank model; lease and occupancy costs sit inside general expenses above profit before tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: the minority interest (R$465m TTM) is folded into the tax/leakage path so that FY0 (PBT x (1 - leakage)) ties to recurring managerial net profit to the parent (R$14,897m TTM). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank, routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md to an equity-flow method -- FCFE at the cost of equity on the component engine (precedent NAB.AX/WFC/USB), NOT an owner-FCF DCF. Deposits and funding are operating liabilities, so net_debt = 0 and nothing is subtracted after the flows. Mapping: revenue = managerial total revenue (NII + fees, R$83,769m TTM: 3Q25 20,760 + 4Q25 21,086 + 1Q26 21,248 + 2Q26 20,675); 'ebitda margin' = profit before tax after provisions, opex, tax expenses and other operating items (TTM 15,756 = 18.8%); D&A and capex = 0 (depreciation is inside general expenses; branch/IT capex is a cost of running the bank, not a growth investment); cash_tax_rate = income tax + social contribution + NCI leakage (TTM only 5.5% because the fixed-R$ IoC deduction and FX-hedge tax effects are large against a depressed PBT); wc_capture_pct = -117.2 is the RETENTION charge: managerial equity / revenue = 98,210 / 83,769 = 1.172, so every R$1 of revenue growth needs R$1.172 of retained equity to hold the CET1 ratio (11.2%, vs ~8% regulatory min+buffers incl. D-SIB -- no excess capital credited). FCFE = net income - retention, which is what can be paid out as IoC + dividends. FY0 FCFE R$9,073m = 14,897 NI - 5,824 (R$98.2bn equity x ~6% steady book growth) -- a notional base, the engine builds year 1 from components. Book basis: managerial BRGAAP equity (R$98.2bn, goodwill only R$1.7bn) rather than IFRS equity (R$125.2bn FY2025, which carries the Banco Real goodwill); the managerial release is the only source for 1H26 and is what ROE guidance is stated on. P/B at the current price ~1.0x managerial book (market cap R$105bn at SANB11 R$28.09 x 3,744M units vs R$98.2bn). One-offs normalized: the 2Q26 R$291m non-recurring labour provision is excluded by using recurring managerial profit; the ~R$700m 2Q26 write-off-methodology/wholesale provisioning hit is left IN the TTM base (conservative) but not extrapolated -- the year-1 margin is set to the 12-15% FY2026 ROE guidance, not the 12.5% 2Q26 run-rate. FY2020 FX-loss/tax-credit distortion only affects the IFRS historical CAGRs. Buybacks: zero cash since FY2022 (R$506m); capital is returned as quarterly IoC (R$2.0bn/qtr in 1H26), so the flat count is the company's real policy, not a convention.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.4% vs revenue 5yr 9.2%: >30% divergence. Revenue 5yr starts from the FX-loss-depressed FY2020 'total income' (R$48.2bn vs R$58.8bn FY2019) and is not representative; 3yr revenue 4.1% and equity 4.3% agree. Equity growth is held down by a 45-60% payout and OCI swings, EPS has de-rated (FY2019 R$2.09 -> FY2025 R$1.63 per share) as credit costs more than doubled (R$13.4bn -> R$29.5bn).
historical_growth.notes: IFRS 20-F series in BRL millions; FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a bank (OCF swings R$-21bn to +R$50bn on deposit and trading flows). Per-share EPS figures are per share; per unit/ADS is 2x.

base.narrative: ROE ~13.5% in year 1 (inside the 12-15% FY2026 guide), 15% in year 2, 16% year 3, settling ~16.3-16.5% from year 4: the mass-market exit and secured-lending mix shift complete, cost of risk normalizes from 3.8% toward ~3.3%, Market NII drag fades as the securities book matures. Revenue growth 3% then 7-8% nominal as Selic easing restarts loan growth, gliding to 6% nominal. Leakage (tax + NCI) rises from 10% to 16% as PBT recovers against a fixed-R$ IoC shield.

bull.narrative: The repositioning works fast: ROE 14.5% in year 1, 17% year 2, ~18.5-19% from year 3 (back to the FY2019 peak economics). Selic falls to low double digits, client spread widens on cheaper funding, cost of risk drops near 3%, SME/cards/Consumer Finance (Webmotors, Toro) drive 9-10% revenue growth, efficiency ratio back under 37% on the branch rationalisation (1,036 -> 858 stores in a year).

bear.narrative: The 2Q26 12.5% ROE is the new normal, not the trough: household indebtedness and rising corporate insolvencies keep cost of risk near 4%, the mass-market retreat costs spread without a matching credit benefit, Market NII stays negative and Nubank/Itau/BTG take share in cards and SME. ROE stuck at ~12-13% -- below the 15% cost of equity, so the bank is worth less than book and every retained real destroys value. Revenue growth 1% then ~5-6% nominal.

scenario_narratives.base: Trough-to-recovery: FY2026 ROE in the 12-15% guided range, a 'more material' recovery in FY2027 as the mass-market exit, secured-lending mix shift and Selic easing pass through, and a mid-teens (~16.5%) mature ROE -- modestly above a 15% BRL cost of equity, which is why the bank is worth slightly more than book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Spread recovery plus credit normalization plus Selic easing all land: ROE back to ~19% (FY2019 levels), 9-10% loan-driven revenue growth, efficiency gains from the branch cut. Requires several independent things to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: Spread compression and elevated credit costs persist: ROE stuck at 12-13%, below the cost of equity, competitive share loss to Nubank/Itau in cards and SME, low single-digit growth. The bank compounds book at a return its owners would not accept.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30%: ROE has fallen four points in two quarters (17.6% -> 12.5%) with NPLs drifting up and the base case resting on a management-promised FY2027 recovery that is not yet in the numbers. Base 50%: the recovery path matches guidance and the deliberate de-risking is visible (store count, mix). Bull 20%: needs spread, credit and Selic to all turn together. Country risk is charged once, in the BRL cost of equity; the weights carry only company-specific trajectory risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth its book value times the spread of sustainable ROE over the cost of equity. BSBR trades at ~1.0x managerial book: the market is pricing ROE roughly equal to a ~15% BRL cost of equity. The base case gives modest upside only because it assumes the FY2027 recovery to mid-teens ROE; the bear case (ROE stuck at 12.5%) is worth ~25% less. All values are computed in BRL and converted to USD per ADS at spot, so a BRL move hits the ADR one-for-one.
key_risks_to_valuation: ROE recovery fails: 2Q26 12.5% ROE persists (cost of risk ~4%, spread compression continues)
BRL depreciation: the ADR value moves one-for-one with USD/BRL; no FX hedge in the model
IoC (interest-on-capital) tax reform reducing or removing the deduction would lift the leakage rate well above 16%
Brazil fiscal stress keeping Selic and long rates high (raises cost of equity, slows loan growth)
Competitive share loss to Nubank, Itau and BTG in cards and SME
Controlling shareholder Santander Spain (~90% economic) sets payout and capital policy; minority float is thin

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (BSBR, NYSE); 52-week range 4.94-7.32. FX Yahoo BRL=X; parity SANB11.SA.
data_sources.financials: BSBR 20-F FY2016-FY2025 (IFRS, BRL millions) via BSBR_Metrics.csv; 3Q25, 4Q25 and 2Q26 managerial earnings releases (6-K) for the TTM revenue, PBT, tax, NCI, recurring net profit, equity, CET1 and share count.
data_sources.qualitative: BSBR_Analysis.json (dcf_notes_for_analyst: NIM direction, cost-of-risk trend, ROE trajectory and FY2026 12-15% guidance, IoC policy, one-offs).

sanity_check_fix.trip: sanity_check.py exit 3: implied P/E 3.3x > 2x 10yr avg 0.9x; implied P/B 0.34x > 1.5x 10yr max 0.17x
sanity_check_fix.fix_applied: none -- trip diagnosed as a checker currency/per-unit artifact, not a valuation error. Both sides of every multiple divide a USD (or doubly FX-converted) per-ADS price by BRL per-SHARE fundamentals (1 ADS = 2 shares): the checker's history says BSBR traded at 0.05-0.17x book and 0.4-1.7x earnings for a decade, which is impossible for a bank that has traded around 1-2x book. Applying a WACC premium or growth cap against that reference would have distorted a model whose currency-consistent multiples sit inside or below BSBR's own range. The diagnosis candidate (wacc_too_low, 'regulatory single point of failure') is already priced: country risk in the 15% BRL cost of equity, IoC reform listed as a key risk, bear weight 30%.

implied_multiples_after_fix.basis: BRL per unit (= per ADS), intrinsic_value_brl against TTM-Jun-26 recurring managerial NP R$3.98/unit, managerial book R$26.23/unit, IFRS FY2025 book R$33.52/unit, TTM revenue R$22.37/unit
